subject: Emitter loses indentation around a source-echo comment in the generated CL
description:
FOUND s446 (README review, while producing a generated-code exhibit for the README).  Cosmetic, not a correctness bug — but it is visible in the first output anyone pastes, and the README now claims the emission is legible.

REPRO (this tree, gen v2-290):

  printf 'my $n = shift // 10;\nmy @sq = map { $_ * $_ } 1 .. $n;\nprint "sum=", eval { my $t = 0; $t += $_ for @sq; $t }, "\n";\n' > /tmp/ex.pl
  ./pl2cl /tmp/ex.pl

The `eval { ... }` body emits:

            (p-my-= $t 0)
            ;; $t += $_ for @sq
  (p-foreach ($_ @sq) (p-incf $t $_))
            $t)))

The `;;` source-echo comment AND the `(p-foreach ...)` form after it are both
written at column 0, inside a block whose surrounding forms are indented to
depth.  Everything else in the file indents correctly, so it looks like the
comment node resets the printer's current indent and the next form inherits
the reset.

WHERE TO LOOK: the CLForm printer (Pl/CLForm.pm) and whatever emits the
statement-echo comment for a statement-modifier `for` inside an eval block.
Note task #132 ("source-echo comments in v2 output") is the related open
question about whether these comments should exist at all — if that is
answered "drop them", this closes with it.

BAR: the exhibit in README.md (the `my $n` / `my @sq` snippet) plus this
repro both indent by depth; no other emission change (corpus-diff IDENTICAL
apart from whitespace).
